subject: Mathematics
name: Mathematics Advanced, Year 12
about: HSC, Calculus, series, random variables and finance
syllabus: NSW Mathematics Advanced 11-12 Syllabus (2024), Year 12 focus areas

points.title: Combining transformations
points.brief: Graphing y = kf(a(x + b)) + c by applying dilations, reflections and translations in the right order, and finding the new position of a point.

points.title: Transforming trigonometric graphs
points.brief: In y = k sin(a(x + b)) + c, k sets the amplitude, 2π/a the period, b the phase shift and c the centre line.

points.title: Modelling with functions
points.brief: Choosing a linear, quadratic, exponential or trigonometric model to fit a situation, such as tides or population, and interpreting its parameters.

points.title: Finding a rule from a graph
points.brief: Working out the equation of a transformed graph from its features, such as its intercepts, turning point or amplitude.

points.title: Arithmetic sequences
points.brief: Each term adds a common difference d. The nth term is a + (n - 1)d.

points.title: Arithmetic series
points.brief: The sum of n terms is n/2 × (2a + (n - 1)d), or n/2 × (first + last).

points.title: Geometric sequences
points.brief: Each term multiplies by a common ratio r. The nth term is arⁿ⁻¹.

points.title: Geometric series
points.brief: The sum of n terms is a(rⁿ - 1)/(r - 1) for r ≠ 1.

points.title: Limiting sums
points.brief: When -1 < r < 1, a geometric series approaches a/(1 - r) as more terms are added. Otherwise it has no limiting sum.

points.title: Sigma notation
points.brief: Σ is shorthand for a sum, with the first and last values of the counter written below and above.

points.title: Derivatives of trigonometric functions
points.brief: The derivative of sin x is cos x, of cos x is -sin x, and of tan x is sec²x, with x in radians, combined with the chain rule.

points.title: Derivatives of exponentials and logarithms
points.brief: The derivative of eᶠ⁽ˣ⁾ is f'(x)eᶠ⁽ˣ⁾, and of ln f(x) is f'(x)/f(x).

points.title: Stationary points
points.brief: Points where f'(x) = 0. A table of gradients either side shows whether each is a maximum, a minimum or a horizontal point of inflection.

points.title: The second derivative and concavity
points.brief: f''(x) > 0 means concave up and f''(x) < 0 means concave down. A point of inflection is where concavity changes.

points.title: Curve sketching with calculus
points.brief: Sketching a function from its intercepts, stationary points, points of inflection and behaviour at the edges of its domain.

points.title: Antiderivatives
points.brief: An antiderivative undoes differentiation. The antiderivative of xⁿ is xⁿ⁺¹/(n + 1) + C for n ≠ -1, and C is the constant of integration.

points.title: Integrals of exponential and trigonometric functions
points.brief: Integrating eˣ, sin x, cos x and sec²x, including with a linear inside such as e³ˣ or cos(2x).

points.title: Integrals giving logarithms
points.brief: The integral of 1/x is ln|x| + C, and the integral of f'(x)/f(x) is ln|f(x)| + C.

points.title: The definite integral
points.brief: The definite integral from a to b is F(b) - F(a), where F is an antiderivative. This is the fundamental theorem of calculus.

points.title: Areas under curves
points.brief: The integral gives signed area. Area below the x-axis is negative, so regions above and below are found separately and added as positive values.

points.title: Area between two curves
points.brief: The area between y = f(x) and y = g(x) is the integral of the upper function minus the lower one, between their intersections.

points.title: The trapezoidal rule
points.brief: Estimating a definite integral by splitting the area into trapezia of equal width and adding their areas.

points.title: Optimisation
points.brief: Writing a quantity as a function of one variable, differentiating and finding the maximum or minimum, then checking the endpoints and the answer makes sense.

points.title: Displacement, velocity and acceleration
points.brief: Velocity is the derivative of displacement and acceleration is the derivative of velocity. Integrating goes the other way, with initial conditions to find the constant.

points.title: Reading motion from graphs
points.brief: Using displacement-time and velocity-time graphs to tell when a particle is at rest, changing direction or speeding up.

points.title: Exponential growth and decay
points.brief: Quantities that change at a rate proportional to their size follow N = N₀eᵏᵗ, growing if k > 0 and decaying if k < 0, as with populations or radioactive decay.

points.title: Rates of change in context
points.brief: Using derivatives to find how fast a quantity, such as the volume of water in a tank, is changing at a given moment.

points.title: Discrete probability distributions
points.brief: A table of each value of a random variable and its probability. The probabilities must add to 1.

points.title: Expected value
points.brief: E(X) = Σ x × P(x), the long-run average of a random variable.

points.title: Variance and standard deviation of a random variable
points.brief: Var(X) = E(X²) - [E(X)]², and the standard deviation is its square root.

points.title: Probability density functions
points.brief: For a continuous variable, probability is the area under a density curve. The function is never negative and the total area is 1.

points.title: Cumulative distribution functions
points.brief: The cumulative distribution function gives P(X ≤ x), found by integrating the density from the lowest value up to x.

points.title: The normal distribution
points.brief: A symmetric bell-shaped distribution set by its mean and standard deviation. About 68%, 95% and 99.7% of values lie within 1, 2 and 3 standard deviations.

points.title: z-scores
points.brief: z = (x - μ)/σ tells how many standard deviations a value is from the mean, so scores from different distributions can be compared.

points.title: Probabilities from the normal distribution
points.brief: Using z-scores with a table or the empirical rule to find the probability that a normal variable lies in an interval.

points.title: Compound interest
points.brief: A = P(1 + r)ⁿ, with r the rate per period and n the number of periods. Interest earns interest.

points.title: Annuities as geometric series
points.brief: An annuity is a series of equal regular payments. Its future value is the sum of a geometric series of compounded payments.

points.title: Present value of an annuity
points.brief: The lump sum needed now to fund a series of future payments, found by discounting each payment.

points.title: Reducing balance loans
points.brief: Each period interest is added and a repayment is taken off. Setting the balance after n periods to zero gives the repayment.

points.title: Using tables of interest factors
points.brief: Reading future or present value interest factors from a table to find the value of an annuity without the full formula.
